hook: What if old maps guide Charleston's 65 acre Union Pier redevelopment?

sections.voiceover: What if old maps guide Charleston's 65 acre Union Pier redevelopment?
b_roll: historic map of Charleston overlaid on waterfront satellite view

sections.voiceover: In Charleston, planners study historic maps along the Cooper River. Early surveys show the walled city ended at Craven's Bastion. Where did expansion reach near Anson Street?
b_roll: historic survey diagram along Cooper River waterfront
archival illustration of Craven's Bastion near Customs House
map zoom toward Anson Street boundary

sections.voiceover: But during the 1920s and 1930s, the city consolidated and cut back Charleston's waterfront for industrial port use.
b_roll: black and white archival footage of 1920s port industrial activity

sections.voiceover: Wharves built in the 18th century extended outward from high ground. Archival research now guides redevelopment across the 65 acre site. Historical records document this waterfront evolution.
b_roll: illustration of 18th century wharves extending into Cooper River
modern site plan map for 65 acre Union Pier
archival document overlay on modern shoreline map

sections.voiceover: Past maps define the future 65 acre site.
b_roll: cinematic motion graphic merging historic map into future site rendering
